## Challenge
Manual row entry makes a valid batch cumbersome and a rejected batch must not leave a partially updated destination.

## Goals
Commit every valid row; if any row is invalid, retain exactly the original destination. Make rejection visible to the user.

## Scope and non-goals
Local batch import only. No remote publication, automatic next-stage execution, network service or change to existing single-row behavior. A runtime storage outage and concurrent writers require their own specified behavior before any broader guarantee is claimed; this fixture selects validation rejection.

## Governing principle
A rejected batch must leave the user where they started.

## Proposed direction
Validate a complete batch before crossing the persistence boundary. Preserve the all-or-nothing outcome for invalid input; Design owns realization.

## Feasibility
The supplied storage interface supports one validated batch write. This is a bounded fixture assumption, not live provider evidence. If that assumption fails, return the constraint and options to the direction owner without weakening the goal.

## Decision requested
Approve this direction for independently reviewed Design work only. This draft grants no Design approval, implementation, publication or merge authority.
","importer/importer.md":"# Importer Design

Model validation contract: model-document-v1

## Introduction and goals
Owner importer combines child Input validation and child Store persistence. Preserve the approved invalid-batch no-write outcome, with one current owner for each child rule and this composed guarantee.

## Architecture constraints
Direction is the exact approved proposal; no remote publication is authorized. Input supplies validated rows; Store accepts the complete validated batch. Installation, public release and outage/concurrency guarantees are outside this bounded fixture.

## Architecture overview
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  User --> Importer
  Importer -->|validate complete batch| Input
  Input -->|validated batch or rejection| Importer
  Importer -->|only validated batch| Store
```
| View | Necessity and reason |
| --- | --- |
| Context | Necessary: local user and destination are external boundaries, shown above. |
| Building Block | Necessary: Importer, Input and Store have different responsibilities, shown above. |
| Runtime | Necessary: rejection must precede any write; sequence below. |
| Deployment | Not necessary: one local process and private destination; no separate service or deployment claim. |

## Requirements
| ID | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| IMPORT-SR-01 | Each row has an integer ID and nonempty value; duplicate IDs within the batch reject. |
| IMPORT-SR-02 | An invalid batch leaves the destination unchanged; a valid batch commits every row. |

### Boundary scan and acceptance scenarios
| Dimension | Requirement basis | Distinct outcome to demonstrate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input domain | IMPORT-SR-01 | Integer/nonempty/duplicate distinctions yield exact acceptance or rejection. |
| State/lifecycle | IMPORT-SR-02 | Invalid input preserves original rows; valid batch adds all rows. |
| Identity/authority | - | Not applicable: local input has no principal/authorization rule in this bounded model. |
| Composition/path | IMPORT-SR-02 | Full validation precedes Store invocation; per-row validation alone cannot prove this. |
| Temporal/retry | - | Not applicable: retries and concurrent writers are explicitly outside this fixture's supported scope. |
| Failure/recovery | IMPORT-SR-01, IMPORT-SR-02 | Invalid middle row gives nonzero rejection and no destination mutation. |
| Compatibility/migration | - | Not applicable: no persisted-format migration or retired operation is introduced. |
| External/environment | IMPORT-SR-02 | Observe the real local destination; no network dependency is claimed. |

## Runtime and interfaces
The importer validates all rows and duplicate IDs before invoking Store once. If the middle row is invalid, it returns a validation failure without invoking Store. The valid batch write adds all three rows to the existing destination. Children do not own the parent's sequencing guarantee.
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  User->>Importer: batch
  Importer->>Input: all rows
  alt invalid row
    Input-->>Importer: rejection
    Importer-->>User: nonzero validation failure
  else all valid
    Input-->>Importer: validated complete batch
    Importer->>Store: write complete batch
    Importer-->>User: complete success
  end
```

## Test design
See [owned coverage](test-design/cases.md). IMPORT-TC-01/02 retain conditions, independent observations and proposed realization here, independently of a Delivery plan. Parent owns the Input-to-Store no-write interaction; per-row checks cannot observe it.

## Decisions and risk
IMPORT-DEC-01 chooses complete validation before write over a validate/write loop: the latter can leave row1 behind after row2 fails. Preserve that alternative and consequence. Unknown protected behavior returns to Design; material infeasibility returns to the direction owner.

## Supporting examples
[Example E0](examples/rejection.md) is an explicitly declared illustration of IMPORT-SR-02, not a workflow record or executed test.

## Limits and handoff
Exact model, coverage and relied-on example go to independent Design Review. Proposed tests are unexecuted. No authored document or save receipt supplies approval.

Model validation contract: model-document-v1

## Introduction and goals
Owner importer combines child Input validation and child Store persistence. Preserve the approved invalid-batch no-write outcome, with one current owner for each child rule and this composed guarantee.

## Architecture constraints
Direction is the exact approved proposal; no remote publication is authorized. Input supplies validated rows; Store accepts the complete validated batch. Installation, public release and outage/concurrency guarantees are outside this bounded fixture.

## Architecture overview
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  User --> Importer
  Importer -->|validate complete batch| Input
  Input -->|validated batch or rejection| Importer
  Importer -->|only validated batch| Store
```
| View | Necessity and reason |
| --- | --- |
| Context | Necessary: local user and destination are external boundaries, shown above. |
| Building Block | Necessary: Importer, Input and Store have different responsibilities, shown above. |
| Runtime | Necessary: rejection must precede any write; sequence below. |
| Deployment | Not necessary: one local process and private destination; no separate service or deployment claim. |

## Requirements
| ID | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| IMPORT-SR-01 | Each row has an integer ID and nonempty value; duplicate IDs within the batch reject. |
| IMPORT-SR-02 | An invalid batch leaves the destination unchanged; a valid batch commits every row. |

### Boundary scan and acceptance scenarios
| Dimension | Requirement basis | Distinct outcome to demonstrate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input domain | IMPORT-SR-01 | Integer/nonempty/duplicate distinctions yield exact acceptance or rejection. |
| State/lifecycle | IMPORT-SR-02 | Invalid input preserves original rows; valid batch adds all rows. |
| Identity/authority | - | Not applicable: local input has no principal/authorization rule in this bounded model. |
| Composition/path | IMPORT-SR-02 | Full validation precedes Store invocation; per-row validation alone cannot prove this. |
| Temporal/retry | - | Not applicable: retries and concurrent writers are explicitly outside this fixture's supported scope. |
| Failure/recovery | IMPORT-SR-01, IMPORT-SR-02 | Invalid middle row gives nonzero rejection and no destination mutation. |
| Compatibility/migration | - | Not applicable: no persisted-format migration or retired operation is introduced. |
| External/environment | IMPORT-SR-02 | Observe the real local destination; no network dependency is claimed. |

## Runtime and interfaces
The importer validates all rows and duplicate IDs before invoking Store once. If the middle row is invalid, it returns a validation failure without invoking Store. The valid batch write adds all three rows to the existing destination. Children do not own the parent's sequencing guarantee.
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  User->>Importer: batch
  Importer->>Input: all rows
  alt invalid row
    Input-->>Importer: rejection
    Importer-->>User: nonzero validation failure
  else all valid
    Input-->>Importer: validated complete batch
    Importer->>Store: write complete batch
    Importer-->>User: complete success
  end
```

## Test design
See [owned coverage](test-design/cases.md). IMPORT-TC-01/02 retain conditions, independent observations and proposed realization here, independently of a Delivery plan. Parent owns the Input-to-Store no-write interaction; per-row checks cannot observe it.

## Decisions and risk
IMPORT-DEC-01 chooses complete validation before write over a validate/write loop: the latter can leave row1 behind after row2 fails. Preserve that alternative and consequence. Unknown protected behavior returns to Design; material infeasibility returns to the direction owner.

## Supporting examples
[Example E0](examples/rejection.md) is an explicitly declared illustration of IMPORT-SR-02, not a workflow record or executed test.

Exact model, coverage and relied-on example go to independent Design Review. Proposed tests are unexecuted. No authored document or save receipt supplies approval.

    "importer/importer.md": "# Importer Design

Model validation contract: model-document-v1

## Introduction and goals
Owner importer combines child Input validation and child Store persistence. Preserve the approved invalid-batch no-write outcome, with one current owner for each child rule and this composed guarantee.

## Architecture constraints
Direction is the exact approved proposal; no remote publication is authorized. Input supplies validated rows; Store accepts the complete validated batch. Installation, public release and outage/concurrency guarantees are outside this bounded fixture.

## Architecture overview
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  User["Local caller"] -->|batch request| Importer
  subgraph ImporterModel["Importer model"]
    Importer["Batch orchestration"] -->|validate complete batch| Input["Input child: row and duplicate rules"]
    Input -->|validated batch or rejection| Importer
    Importer -->|only validated batch| Store
    Store["Store child: validated batch persistence"]
  end
  Store -->|apply validated rows| Destination["Existing local destination"]
  Importer -->|complete success or validation rejection| User
```
The model owns the orchestration and its two child responsibilities; the caller and destination are external interfaces. Detailed owners are the [context](#context-view), [building blocks](#building-block-view) and [runtime](#runtime-and-interfaces), rather than this summary alone.

| View | Necessity and reason | Owning detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Context | Necessary: local caller, accepted direction and destination have distinct external roles. | [Context view](#context-view) |
| Building Block | Necessary: orchestration, input validation and persistence have different duties and their composition can fail. | [Building Block view](#building-block-view) |
| Runtime | Necessary: rejection must precede any write. | [Runtime and interfaces](#runtime-and-interfaces) |
| Deployment | Not necessary: one local process/private destination; no separately deployed service or environment-specific guarantee is selected. | Architecture constraints; adding concurrency or outage behavior requires reassessment. |

## Context view
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Direction["Approved direction owner"] -.->|invalid input must preserve prior records| ImporterSystem["Importer"]
  Caller["Local caller"] -->|complete input batch| ImporterSystem
  ImporterSystem -->|success or specific validation rejection| Caller
  ImporterSystem -->|validated batch updates only| Destination["Existing local destination"]
```
The caller submits data and receives the actual result; it does not bypass validation. The direction owner defines the supported invalid-input guarantee and remains the recipient of material infeasibility. The local destination begins with independent prior records and may change only after complete validation. Network publication and outage/concurrency semantics are outside the selected contract.

## Building Block view
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Batch["Public batch interface"] -->|entire request| Orchestrator["Importer orchestration"]
  Orchestrator -->|all rows and IDs| Validator["Input child"]
  Validator -->|validated whole batch or defined rejection| Orchestrator
  Orchestrator -->|one complete validated batch after success| Writer["Store child"]
  Writer -->|apply rows| LocalRecords["Local destination"]
  Orchestrator -->|actual completion or rejection| Result["Caller result"]
```
Input owns integer-ID, nonempty-value and within-batch duplicate checks under IMPORT-SR-01. Store owns the stipulated local operation accepting one complete validated batch; it does not decide input acceptance or authorize partial imports. Importer owns the invocation order and caller result under IMPORT-SR-02 and IMPORT-DEC-01. Neither child's isolated proof establishes that the public importer waits for complete validation; that interaction needs the real destination observations in C0.

## Requirements
| ID | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| IMPORT-SR-01 | Each row has an integer ID and nonempty value; duplicate IDs within the batch reject. |
| IMPORT-SR-02 | An invalid batch leaves the destination unchanged; a valid batch commits every row. |

### Boundary scan and acceptance scenarios
| Dimension | Requirement basis | Distinct outcome to demonstrate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Input domain | IMPORT-SR-01 | Integer/nonempty/duplicate distinctions yield exact acceptance or rejection. |
| State/lifecycle | IMPORT-SR-02 | Invalid input preserves original rows; valid batch adds all rows. |
| Identity/authority | - | Not applicable: local input has no principal/authorization rule in this bounded model. |
| Composition/path | IMPORT-SR-02 | Full validation precedes Store invocation; per-row validation alone cannot prove this. |
| Temporal/retry | - | Not applicable: retries and concurrent writers are explicitly outside this fixture's supported scope. |
| Failure/recovery | IMPORT-SR-01, IMPORT-SR-02 | Invalid middle row gives nonzero rejection and no destination mutation. |
| Compatibility/migration | - | Not applicable: no persisted-format migration or retired operation is introduced. |
| External/environment | IMPORT-SR-02 | Observe the real local destination; no network dependency is claimed. |

## Runtime and interfaces
The importer validates all rows and duplicate IDs before invoking Store once. If the middle row is invalid, it returns a validation failure without invoking Store. The valid batch write adds all three rows to the existing destination. Children do not own the parent's sequencing guarantee.
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  User->>Importer: batch
  Importer->>Input: all rows
  alt invalid row
    Input-->>Importer: rejection
    Importer-->>User: nonzero validation failure
  else all valid
    Input-->>Importer: validated complete batch
    Importer->>Store: write complete batch
    Importer-->>User: complete success
  end
```

## Test design
See [owned coverage](test-design/cases.md). IMPORT-TC-01/02 retain conditions, independent observations and proposed realization here, independently of a Delivery plan. Parent owns the Input-to-Store no-write interaction; per-row checks cannot observe it.

## Decisions and risk
IMPORT-DEC-01 chooses complete validation before write over a validate/write loop: the latter can leave row1 behind after row2 fails. Preserve that alternative and consequence. Unknown protected behavior returns to Design; material infeasibility returns to the direction owner.

## Supporting examples
[Example E0](examples/rejection.md) is an explicitly declared illustration of IMPORT-SR-02, not a workflow record or executed test.

## Limits and handoff
Exact model, coverage and relied-on example go to independent Design Review. Proposed tests are unexecuted. No authored document or save receipt supplies approval.

## Introduction and goals
Owner importer combines child Input validation and child Store persistence. Preserve the approved invalid-batch no-write outcome, with one current owner for each child rule and this composed guarantee.

## Architecture constraints
Direction is the exact approved proposal; no remote publication is authorized. Input supplies validated rows; Store accepts the complete validated batch. Installation, public release and outage/concurrency guarantees are outside this bounded fixture.

## Architecture overview
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  User["Local caller"] -->|batch request| Importer
  subgraph ImporterModel["Importer model"]
    Importer["Batch orchestration"] -->|validate complete batch| Input["Input child: row and duplicate rules"]
    Input -->|validated batch or rejection| Importer
    Importer -->|only validated batch| Store
    Store["Store child: validated batch persistence"]
  end
  Store -->|apply validated rows| Destination["Existing local destination"]
  Importer -->|complete success or validation rejection| User
```
The model owns the orchestration and its two child responsibilities; the caller and destination are external interfaces. Detailed owners are the [context](#context-view), [building blocks](#building-block-view) and [runtime](#runtime-and-interfaces), rather than this summary alone.

| View | Necessity and reason | Owning detail |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Context | Necessary: local caller, accepted direction and destination have distinct external roles. | [Context view](#context-view) |
| Building Block | Necessary: orchestration, input validation and persistence have different duties and their composition can fail. | [Building Block view](#building-block-view) |
| Runtime | Necessary: rejection must precede any write. | [Runtime and interfaces](#runtime-and-interfaces) |
| Deployment | Not necessary: one local process/private destination; no separately deployed service or environment-specific guarantee is selected. | Architecture constraints; adding concurrency or outage behavior requires reassessment. |

## Context view
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Direction["Approved direction owner"] -.->|invalid input must preserve prior records| ImporterSystem["Importer"]
  Caller["Local caller"] -->|complete input batch| ImporterSystem
  ImporterSystem -->|success or specific validation rejection| Caller
  ImporterSystem -->|validated batch updates only| Destination["Existing local destination"]
```
The caller submits data and receives the actual result; it does not bypass validation. The direction owner defines the supported invalid-input guarantee and remains the recipient of material infeasibility. The local destination begins with independent prior records and may change only after complete validation. Network publication and outage/concurrency semantics are outside the selected contract.

## Building Block view
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Batch["Public batch interface"] -->|entire request| Orchestrator["Importer orchestration"]
  Orchestrator -->|all rows and IDs| Validator["Input child"]
  Validator -->|validated whole batch or defined rejection| Orchestrator
  Orchestrator -->|one complete validated batch after success| Writer["Store child"]
  Writer -->|apply rows| LocalRecords["Local destination"]
  Orchestrator -->|actual completion or rejection| Result["Caller result"]
```
Input owns integer-ID, nonempty-value and within-batch duplicate checks under IMPORT-SR-01. Store owns the stipulated local operation accepting one complete validated batch; it does not decide input acceptance or authorize partial imports. Importer owns the invocation order and caller result under IMPORT-SR-02 and IMPORT-DEC-01. Neither child's isolated proof establishes that the public importer waits for complete validation; that interaction needs the real destination observations in C0.

## Requirements
| ID | Required behavior |
| --- | --- |
| IMPORT-SR-01 | Each row has an integer ID and nonempty value; duplicate IDs within the batch reject. |
| IMPORT-SR-02 | An invalid batch leaves the destination unchanged; a valid batch commits every row. |

| --- | --- | --- |
| Input domain | IMPORT-SR-01 | Integer/nonempty/duplicate distinctions yield exact acceptance or rejection. |

## Runtime and interfaces
The importer validates all rows and duplicate IDs before invoking Store once. If the middle row is invalid, it returns a validation failure without invoking Store. The valid batch write adds all three rows to the existing destination. Children do not own the parent's sequencing guarantee.
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  User->>Importer: batch
  Importer->>Input: all rows
  alt invalid row
    Input-->>Importer: rejection
    Importer-->>User: nonzero validation failure
  else all valid
    Input-->>Importer: validated complete batch
    Importer->>Store: write complete batch
    Importer-->>User: complete success
  end
```

## Decisions and risk
IMPORT-DEC-01 chooses complete validation before write over a validate/write loop: the latter can leave row1 behind after row2 fails. Preserve that alternative and consequence. Unknown protected behavior returns to Design; material infeasibility returns to the direction owner.
